summary: deploy.sh: pre-restart guard asserting guru can write the cache, fail loud
description: Add a hard check in deploy/deploy.sh before 'systemctl restart guru-web': assert the runtime user can create+write a file under the cache path, e.g. sudo -u guru /usr/bin/test -w /srv/guru-web/next-cache && sudo -u guru /bin/touch /srv/guru-web/next-cache/.deploy-writecheck (rm after), exit non-zero with a clear message otherwise. This is the regression test: any future ownership/path drift that would reintroduce the EACCES fails the deploy loudly instead of shipping a broken guest /ask. Depends on 60219f46. Done: guard added + committed; verified it exits non-zero when the dir is intentionally made unwritable.

resolution.note: Added pre-restart guard: aborts the deploy (exit 1) unless $RELEASE/.next/cache is a symlink to /srv/guru-web/next-cache AND that dir is owned by guru and owner-writable. Verified all branches via scratchpad guardtest.sh: missing-link/wrong-target/non-writable all rc=1, good case rc=0. is-active can't catch this (process boots, only 500s per-request), so this is the regression test that keeps the EACCES from ever silently shipping again.
